newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury rolls out self-scan to more stores.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury rolls out self-scan to more stores.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc plans to roll out self-scanning to up to 100 stores this year, a statement from the company said.

Sainsbury started trials of self-scanning -- where customers use a hand-held machine to register their own shopping as they move around the store -- at its Camberley, Surrey, southern England store last November.
The aim of self-scanning is to cut down checkout queues and it is already being used in selected stores by Safeway.

Sainsbury said that it would extend trials initially to a further five stores by Easter and then introduce the system in others, hoping that "by the end of the year, customers at up to 100 stores could benefit from this technology."
